text:
Alex P.: Heads-up — follow-up on the 03/18 p95 latency spike. Postmortem is in progress but we need to lock remediation owners and decide if we should temporarily adjust SLO thresholds while we fix the root cause.
Marta V.: +1. We should split owner responsibilities: infra/autoscale and runtime/KV cache.
Samir K.: I can take runtime/KV cache. I saw stale cache eviction and hot-shard behavior in traces. I can put up a prototype fix and load test in ~72h.
Li Wei: I’ll own autoscaling policy and the throttling guardrails. My plan: tighten the scale-up cooldown, add a short burst counter, and adjust the p95 alert to reduce noise. Will need dashboard tiles updated.
Alex P.: Great. Can we also agree on a temporary SLO tweak? Current p95 target is 200ms, we hit 420ms during the incident. Proposal: rebaseline p95 target to 280ms for the next 2-week window while fixes roll out, then re-evaluate. This avoids premature error-budget burns for customers. Thoughts?
Marta V.: I’m wary of changing customer-facing SLOs mid-cycle. What about an internal "buffered SLO" used for oncall/ops calculation, and keep public SLO but mark the window as an incident-affected period?
Samir K.: That sounds safe. We can add a temporary internal SLO = 280ms and flag the incident window in the public SLO dashboard. I’ll include the flag in the PR.
Li Wei: Agreed. I’ll update the alerting rule too. Proposed alert snippet: 
```
alert: HighP95LatencyBuffered
expr: job:service_p95_latency_ms{service="inference"} > 280
for: 5m
labels: {severity: "page"}
annotations: {runbook: "https://go/redwood/runbooks/kv-autoscale"}
```
I’ll push the change to staging dashboards first.
Alex P.: Good. Action items and owners: Samir -> runtime PR + load test (3d), Li Wei -> alert + autoscale policy update (2d), Marta -> public SLO note + customer comm draft (2d), Alex -> coordinate canary and rollback plan (1d). Please add each item to the postmortem ticket and tag @oncall for rollout windows.
OncallBot: Incident 2026-03-18 | error budget burn: 4.2% of monthly budget | current p95: 312ms | linked runbook: https://go/redwood/incident/2026-0318
Marta V.: I created the tickets and assigned owners. Added a dashboard link: https://dash.redwood/s/ops/p95-rebaseline (internal). Please add ETA comments to the ticket.
Samir K.: PR opened draft: https://git.redwood/runtime/pulls/1423 — includes trace annotations and KV eviction tweak. Running perf job now.
Li Wei: Autoscale draft PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/980 — includes cooldown and burst counter. Staging dashboards updated, canary ready once Samir's perf numbers look good.
Alex P.: Thanks all. Quick checklist before canary: (1) update internal SLO window docs, (2) set canary to 5% of traffic, (3) pre-approved rollback condition: p95>350ms for 10m or error-rate up 0.5%. If anyone has concerns ping me now.
Marta V.: No objections. I’ll follow up with CS on the customer note and link it in the public SLO timeline.
Samir K.: Perf job completed — baseline improvement ~18% in tail. Will finalize patch in the morning.
Li Wei: Ready for canary after patch merge. Scheduling 10:00 UTC tomorrow for 5% canary.
Alex P.: OK, recording this as closure items in the postmortem. We’ll reconvene after canary and decide whether to keep the internal buffered SLO or restore original thresholds. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
